Government Exam Photo and Signature Size

Online forms for government exams usually ask for a photograph and a signature as separate JPEG files, each inside a size range in KB. Pick the range from your notification, add your files, and check the result.

Size ranges last reviewed: 2026-10-04. Always confirm against your exam notification.

Compression tool

Target size Target size:
Exam range: Targets sit a little below the maximum. Check your notice.
Advanced settings

By default the tool keeps quality reasonable (about 62% or higher) and reduces dimensions to reach small targets; tick “Keep dimensions” to prefer full size at lower quality. Aspect ratio is always preserved and images are never enlarged. PNG is lossless and may not reach a small target; JPEG/WebP are lossy. JPEG replaces transparency with white; WebP and PNG keep it.

What these forms usually ask for

Requirements change with every notification. The ranges on this page are figures commonly reported for recent 2026 notices by exam-preparation websites, and the sources do not always agree. We have not verified them against each official PDF, so always follow the notification or instructions on the official application portal for your exam.

In general, exam portals ask for a JPEG photograph, a JPEG signature, a size range with both a minimum and a maximum, and sometimes pixel dimensions. Recent notices from several recruiting bodies have also moved to capturing the photograph live through a webcam or phone camera during the application, so check whether you need to upload a photo file at all.

Using the range presets

The tool has presets named after the size range, such as 10–20 KB or 20–50 KB. Each preset sets a target slightly below the top of the range and remembers the minimum, so you can see a warning if a result comes out too small. The target is deliberately a little under the maximum because this site counts 1KB as 1,024 bytes, while some portals count 1,000 bytes. Aiming a few KB lower avoids a rejection for being one kilobyte over.

Exam-by-exam pages

For more detail, see the pages for SSC, RRB (railway) and UPSC. Bank exams such as IBPS and SBI are commonly reported with a photograph of about 20–50 KB and a signature of about 10–20 KB, while NTA exams such as NEET and JEE Main are reported with wider ranges and extra items such as a thumb impression or a postcard-size photo. State public service commissions and private employers publish their own limits, so use the custom size box when your range is different.

Photo and signature are separate files

Run the photograph and the signature separately, because they usually have different ranges. A signature on white paper is mostly empty space, so it compresses to a very small file. If the result is below the minimum, scan or photograph the signature at a larger size, and avoid cropping so tightly that little remains.

Pixel dimensions

Some notices give pixel sizes, while others give centimetres, and the figures differ between sources. This tool keeps the aspect ratio and only reduces dimensions, so it fits your image inside a width and height you set under Advanced settings. It does not crop or stretch. Crop to the correct shape in your phone’s editor first, then compress here.

Before you submit

Check the file format is a real JPEG, the file name follows the portal’s rules, the size is within the range, the face or signature is clear, and the photo has a plain background if the notice demands one. Keep the original files, because a later stage of the process may ask for them again.

Privacy for identity photos

Photographs and signatures are personal. The compression happens in your browser and nothing is uploaded for processing. Delete the downloaded files from shared computers when you finish.

Common questions

Which size range should I choose?

The one printed in your exam notification or on the upload screen. Each exam and each year can differ, so do not rely on memory or on another candidate’s form.

My result is below the minimum size. What now?

Use a larger or sharper original, crop less tightly, tick Keep dimensions, or raise the target. A signature on plain paper can be very small, so a higher-resolution scan helps.
